anzsic_codes.name: Computer System Design and Related Services

merger_description:
TD SYNNEX Corporation, via its wholly-owned subsidiary Sky Meets River, Inc., proposes to acquire up to 100% of the share capital in United Radio Incorporated, trading as BlueStar, Inc. (**BlueStar**) (the **Acquisition**).

TD SYNNEX Corporation (together with its subsidiaries, **TDS**), is a global wholesale distributor of IT products and solutions. TDS distributes a broad range of IT products and related services to resellers, value-added resellers, managed service providers, systems integrators and other channel partners. This includes:

* end-point computing products (e.g. desktops, laptops, smartphones and peripherals)
* enterprise infrastructure (e.g. servers)
* networking and communications products, software (including software-as-a-service, cloud and cybersecurity solutions), and
* office printing products and consumables.

BlueStar is a specialist value-added technology distributor. Its business is focused principally on products and solutions (such as barcode scanners, point-of-sale computers, radio-frequency identification products, commercial digital signage, visitor management systems) used in retail, hospitality, warehousing, logistics, healthcare, field service and physical-security applications. BlueStar’s customers are generally value-added resellers, systems integrators and other channel partners that use these products to deliver integrated solutions to end users in particular industry verticals.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, including market share
data from prior matters, the ACCC considers that the Acquisition is
unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of competition given:
a. BlueStar has a small presence in Australia
b. the parties’ combined share in the wholesale supply and
distribution of IT products in Australia to customers in
Australia is low and the increase in share of supply arising
from the Acquisition would be small
c. there are alternative wholesaler suppliers and distributors of
IT products to customers in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
